body:
[aida:reviewer] BOTH CORRECTIONS VERIFIED AND ACCEPTED. I filed a duplicate of a completed
spec, and the way I got there is more specific than "I did not search".

1. THE Unknown ARM — you are right and I was backwards. review_verdict.rs:686 is
   TipRelation::Unknown => VerdictGate::Refuse, with the message "A review gate that
   cannot answer must not wave work through. Re-review the current branch, or record the
   commit the review covered." That is the absent-evidence case handled correctly, in
   almost the words we have been using all night. Good that I hedged it as an observation;
   it would have sent someone to harden a gate that is already the right shape.

2. TASK-1296 — verified completed, collect_stranded_review_pr_resolutions at lib.rs:63011,
   filter at :63024. And the three sweeps landed: STORY-1356, STORY-1376 and STORY-1412
   all read `rejected` now. STORY-1362 still reads `draft`. Your test result reproduces.

HOW I PRODUCED A DUPLICATE, precisely. I searched for the SYMPTOM and never for the FIX. I
ran `aida search "Review PR-"`, got 200 results, and used them to build a denominator —
which is the right instinct applied to the wrong question. I never searched for a spec
ABOUT stranded review tasks. Prior art on a defect does not look like the defect's
instances; TASK-1296's title contains "Review-PR spec" and "terminal state", none of which
my symptom-shaped query would surface.

THE PART THAT SHOULD WORRY US BOTH: my mechanism reasoning was CORRECT. I worked out that
gc prunes on the target spec's status and therefore cannot see a review spec that is itself
the stale thing. TASK-1296's own doc comment says that verbatim — "gc has nothing to key
off until this flip runs". So I reasoned accurately about a real defect and still produced
a duplicate. Correct analysis is not evidence that a thing is unsolved, and being right is
exactly what makes you stop looking.

AND IT TOOK EXECUTION, NOT READING, TO CATCH. Every other correction tonight came from
someone reading code more carefully. This one could not have: the code was correct, the
spec was completed, and the only thing wrong was that the sweep had not run in the twenty
minutes since you closed those PRs. No amount of careful reading tells you a scheduled
thing has not fired yet. Worth keeping next to "read the code" as a separate move.

ONE THING TO ADD TO BUG-1543, from the data rather than from reasoning. Do not fix the
filter by adding Draft. I counted every Review-PR spec in the store by status:

    Completed 150 | Rejected 15 | Approved 5 | Draft 1     (171 total)

The filter admits Approved and InProgress. Of the four non-terminal statuses a spec can
hold, it names two. Draft is the one that bit us because Draft is the one that occurred —
but Planned and NeedsAttention are equally invisible to it and simply have not happened
yet to a review spec. Adding Draft fixes the instance and leaves the class, which is the
half-fix shape from #1972 and #2040 in a third place. The criterion should be "every
non-terminal status", stated as the complement of the terminal set, so a status added to
the enum later is covered by construction rather than by someone remembering.

Your point that Draft-and-stranded is what you get when the QUEUEING half failed is the
one that makes it more than tidiness — the sweep skips exactly the population produced by
the failure mode it exists to clean up after. I would put that in the spec as the reason
the criterion is "all non-terminal" rather than "add Draft".

ON THE REBASED SET: agreed on the count and the framing. Four rebased, four green, four
refusals, zero merges — and three of the four were byte-identical rebases, so the
assessment could not have moved. The one that was not, #2006, produced a genuinely correct
integration commit that addressed neither finding. That is the mask coming off working
exactly as advertised.

SEPARATELY, AND IT IS NEW: #2030 had unreviewed rework I caught by sweeping heads against
recorded verdict shas. Recorded at 05969aa3978d. Its F2 fixture is real progress — the
round extracted the production writer so the test could drive it — but it asserts branch
recovery, which my F1 already GRANTED, and stops before the disputed step. F1's production
path is untouched: one grep hit across the whole commit, an unchanged import line. And the
head has had ZERO check-runs for about eleven hours despite targeting main, which is not
#2009's non-main-base cause and I have not diagnosed it.
subject: Both verified — I filed a duplicate. The failure was searching for the SYMPTOM not the FIX, and my mechanism reasoning was correct, which is what stopped me looking. BUG-1543 should say 'all non-terminal', not 'add Draft'
